title: Pricing Cross-Bank Context in Federated Anti-Money Laundering
abstract: arXiv:2610.35996v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Most graph-based Anti-Money Laundering (AML) methods assume access to a pooled transaction graph containing all accounts and payments, which in reality does not exist. Federated learning offers the necessary privacy guarantees but it remains unclear how money laundering patterns spanning separate graphs can effectively be detected. We exploit transactions already recorded by both endpoint banks to approximate remote account states locally, enabling multi-layer Graph Neural Network (GNN) computation without additional account-specific exchange. Starting from this baseline, we test whether the remaining context is worth sharing, using a disclosure ladder that adds two transaction counts per remote account or the counterparty's own GNN states. translated_title: 联邦反洗钱中跨银行上下文信息的定价
translated_abstract: 大多数基于图的反洗钱（AML）方法都假设可以访问一个包含所有账户和支付信息的集中式交易图，但这种情况在现实中并不存在。联邦学习能够提供必要的隐私保障，然而跨越多个独立图的洗钱模式如何被有效检测仍不清楚。我们利用交易双方银行已经记录的交易，在本地近似远程账户的状态，从而无需额外的账户级信息交换即可实现多层图神经网络（GNN）计算。以此作为基线，我们通过一个信息披露阶梯来测试剩余的上下文信息是否值得共享：为每个远程账户增加两个交易计数，或共享对手方自身的GNN状态。在AMLworld HI-Small数据集上，跨越六种GNN骨干网络和多达32个数据孤岛的实验表明，可观测基线带来了最大的性能提升，并且随着数据碎片化导致可见部分缩小，这一优势依然保持；交易计数则带来了稳健的修正提升。
tldr: 该论文提出利用交易双方银行已记录的交易在本地近似远程账户状态，实现无需额外隐私数据交换的联邦多层GNN反洗钱检测，并通过信息披露阶梯实验发现可观测基线已贡献最大收益，额外共享的跨银行上下文信息边际价值有限。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes locally approximating remote account states using transactions already recorded by both endpoint banks, enabling multi-layer GNN federated anti-money laundering detection without extra private data exchange, and finds via a disclosure ladder that the observable baseline yields the largest gain while sharing additional cross-bank context offers limited marginal value.
